sample_unit: biopsy-naïve patients (MRI data from four centres)

links.outcome: AI diagnostic AUC for clinically significant PCa versus 11 general radiologists on same data
links.effect: PI-RADS-AI outperformed 5/11 (45.5%) and matched 3/11 (27.3%) general radiologists; AUC internal 0.801 vs 0.770, p<0.01; external 0.833 vs 0.867, p=0.309.
links.quote: In the paired test, PI-RADS<sup>AI</sup> outperformed 5/11 (45.5%) and matched the performance of 3/11 (27.3%) general radiologists in achieving a clinically significant PCa diagnosis (area under the curve, internal test, 0.801 vs. 0.770, p < 0.01; external test, 0.833 vs. 0.867, p = 0.309).

links.outcome: Agreement with subspecialist in internal versus external tests; multicentre versus single-centre training
links.effect: Triple-centre model kappa 0.716 vs 0.531 for single-centre; agreement 58.4% (188/322) internal and 60.1% (92/153) external.
links.quote: In the ablation experiment, the model trained with the data from three centres was superior (kappa coefficient, 0.716 vs. 0.531) to that trained with single-centre data.

unlisted_practices: training AI with subspecialist knowledge-guided human-in-the-loop two-stage architecture
multicentre training data to improve generalizability

screen.reason: Evaluates a deep-learning model for prostate cancer MRI diagnosis comparing its performance to general radiologists in a multi-center retrospective validation and reader study, but does not test an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
